paper_title: Denotational Semantics for Stabiliser Quantum Programs
classifications: Theory of computation → Quantum computation theory
statement: We conjecture that full abstraction extends to a language with arbitrary (non-affine) classical control, with respect to the equivalence induced by possible measurement outcomes.
context: We have given a sound, universal, and complete denotational semantics for stabiliser quantum programs in terms of affine relations over finite fields, including measurement, classically controlled Pauli operators, and affine classical computation. For odd prime dimensions this covers all stabiliser operations; for qubits, it is restricted to CSS stabiliser operations. The resulting relational semantics reflects the algebraic structure underlying stabiliser quantum error correction, and is conceptually transparent and computationally tractable compared to general denotational models for quantum programs. We demonstrated the semantics with a fully abstract denotational semantics for the assembly language SPL. We conjecture that full abstraction extends to a language with arbitrary (non-affine) classical control, with respect to the equivalence induced by possible measurement outcomes. It is natural future work to explore a graphical presentation of these semantics via the ZX-calculus, for which a complete calculus for affine Lagrangian relations already exists [9]. The ZX-calculus has already been applied to the construction of fault-tolerant quantum circuits [8] and to the design and verification of QEC codes [15, 21].
